title: Email: Fw: New protocol: Filing stories

content.text:
Anthony Fenech
Tigers beat writer
Detroit Free Press
(734) 752-9667
Twitter: @anthonyfenech
From: Thomas, Christopher <cdthomas@freepress.com>
Sent: Saturday, April 18, 2020 9:18 PM
To: Albom, Mitch <malbom@freepress.com>; Alter, Marlowe <malter@freepress.com>; Birkett, David <dbirkett@freepress.com>; Crawford, Kirkland <kcrawford@freepress.com>; Sankofa, Omari <OSankofa@freepress.com>; Fenech, Anthony <afenech@freepress.com>; Ford, Ryan <rford@freepress.com>; Monarrez, Carlos <cmonarrez@freepress.com>; Sabin, Rainer <RSabin@freepress.com>; Sang, Orion <OSang@freepress.com>; Seidel, Jeff <jseidel@freepress.com>; Solari, Chris <CSOLARI@lsj.com>; St. James, Helene <hstjames@freepress.com>; Sung, Elaine <ESung@freepress.com>; Windsor, Shawn <swindsor@freepress.com>
Cc: Manzullo, Brian <bmanzullo@freepress.com>; Delgado, Anjanette <adelgado@freepress.com>; Byrne, Patrick <pbyrne@freepress.com>
Subject: New protocol: Filing stories 
 
Hey, guys: I’m adding an addendum to how we file stories to help us prioritize work on the web desk.
Given the furloughs, this system should help us make quick decisions regardless who is working. It also should help us decide when to publish non-breaking stories for optimum results.
Let’s start using it immediately. Feel free to reach out to me individually with any concerns.
The gist: With each story, include one of the following indicators in the subject line:
BREAKING: Urgent breaking news story. The desk should immediately read, post and social the story. There should be discussion about potential push alert.
Example: Personnel moves, firings, hirings, arrests, deaths, big scoops, major injuries, etc.
COMPETITIVE: Time-sensitive story that other outlets are also pursuing. Producers grabbing stories should grab these before anything below.
Example: News conference updates, injury reports, scrums, news alerts in press releases, etc.
TIMELY: Non-breaking, non-competitive story of high value and interest. Likely to receive prominent placement across several platforms.
Example: Enterprise, features, mailbags, non-breaking columns and non-breaking “main bars.”.
EMBARGO: Can’t be published immediately. The embargo should be accompanied by a time on the email. If not, an editor should be consulted by producer for publish time (or consult digital plan).
Example: Next-day analyses, morning columns, Sunday enterprise/features, some breaking news, etc.
EVERGREEN: Material planned in advance that is lower priority and but has potential for high impact.
Example: Advance content before a vacation, any story that has no definite time peg.
ADVANCE OBIT: An advance obit that needs to be read and filed for later.
NEW PROTOCOL FAQ
What prompted this change?

Good question. Now that we’re working remotely, we’ve had some issues with stories being published without much discussion. This is particularly true for posts filed overnight and handled by webmizz. So, we’ve asked webmizz to only publish breaking news filed overnight or early in the morning before the Sports staff arrives. These classifications will make it clear which stories they can grab.
If I pick a time for my story to be embargoed, will it be changed?

As we do with all copy, the web desk will move stories around based on audience trends and availability for best exposure. So, a story filed a TIMELY story filed at noon might be held for the next morning if there’s a flood of other content that may overshadow it. Likewise, a story filed as EMBARGO may get published immediately if we’re in a light news day. The purpose of these new indicators is to serve as a starting point for the desk.
How does this addendum affect the digital budget?

Another good question. It doesn’t impact the digital budget. You should still place stories on the digital budget for the day you expect it to publish. The desk will move stories around on the budget if plans change. ​
This new protocol is confusing and makes no sense. What should I do?

When in doubt, talk through it with an editor. There will be some adjustment as we figure out exactly how to classify each story, but we’ll get there. Just remember: These classifications are a starting point. If you think something is urgent (or wherever it falls on the spectrum), then make sure we know it, too.
Should you bug webmizz to post a story?
If it’s not breaking, don’t bug webmizz. Call an editor. Our webmizz team is busy optimizing stories for news side and all our pandemic coverage. They are busy.
Chris Thomas
Sports editor, Detroit Free Press
Great Lakes regional sports director, USA TODAY Network
cdthomas@freepress.com
